summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, recurrent pulmonary emboli, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and a 40-pound weight gain over one month. Initial concern for pulmonary embolism was raised due to subtherapeutic INR of 1.5, but CT angiography ruled out central PE, though image quality limited exclusion of peripheral clots. She was bridged with heparin and restarted on warfarin, reaching a therapeutic INR of 2.3 by discharge. Her symptoms were attributed to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbated by fluid retention, likely related to steroid use. She received IV furosemide with improvement in symptoms and weight reduction to 425 lbs, her baseline. Her home furosemide was increased to twice daily, and metoprolol was slightly increased, though limited by blood pressure. Polymyositis remained stable, with elevated but stable CK and downtrending troponin. She was discharged with instructions to monitor weight, avoid high-salt foods, check BMP in one week, and follow up with her primary care and cardiology providers.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
